title: A week in my life
prompt: Write about an invented student’s daily life and jobs at home. Include a birthday date, a school routine, three chores and words showing how often the student does them.
checks: I used present simple forms correctly.
I included an ordinal number in a date.
I used frequency words in clear positions.
I included one negative sentence.

title: Usually and right now
prompt: Imagine a school trip to a farm or wildlife park. Describe three animals and what people are doing now. Contrast one action with a usual routine and include a rule with must.
checks: I named animals and at least one young animal.
I used am/is/are + -ing for now.
I used present simple for a usual action.
I used object pronouns and must accurately.

title: A holiday message
prompt: Write a short message about an imagined past holiday. Say where you went, how you travelled, where you stayed and what you did. Include a small problem and how the trip ended.
checks: I used was or were correctly.
I included regular and irregular past forms.
I used didn’t with a base verb.
I asked one past simple question.

title: A picnic recipe
prompt: Invent a simple dish for a picnic. List the ingredients with clear quantities, then write the steps in order. Use a/an, some/any and a little/a few where they fit.
checks: I made countable and uncountable quantities clear.
I used containers or measurements where useful.
I used base verbs for instructions.
I organized the steps with first, then and next.

title: Compare three places
prompt: Invent three holiday places and a small table of prices or distances. Compare the places with comparative and superlative adjectives. Describe the weather and add one as … as comparison.
checks: I labelled my places and data as imaginary.
I used than in comparative sentences.
I used the with superlatives.
I included a clear as … as comparison.

title: Make a weekend plan
prompt: Write a conversation arranging a weekend activity with an invented friend. Make suggestions, agree a place and time, and explain one thing each person has to do first. Describe how someone does an activity using an adverb.
checks: I used going to for plans.
I used have to or don’t have to for obligations.
I included a suggestion and a suitable reply.
I chose adjectives and adverbs accurately.
